image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a white and teal steam iron resting on a soft, light purple fabric surface. The image focuses on the soleplate, which features a grid of green-rimmed steam holes. The body is white plastic with teal accents, including a handle grip and control buttons. A power cord is partially visible at the rear base.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The green rings around the steam holes appear slightly painted-on or decal-like rather than physically recessed or integrated into the metal, lacking realistic depth shadows inside the holes.
The background fabric has a very uniform, soft-focus blur that lacks natural fiber detail, typical of AI-generated bokeh, but not structurally damaging.
The power cord merges into the base of the iron without a clear strain relief or plug housing; it appears to melt slightly into the plastic casing.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific type of iron and rule out misclassification as similar appliances (e.g., garment steamer).
To check for edge bleeding between the metallic soleplate and the plastic body, and to verify the integrity of the steam hole boundaries.
To verify if the steam holes have actual depth (recessed) or are flat textures, and to ensure the handle connects logically to the body in 3D space.

focus_areas: Realism of steam hole depth and integration
Connection point of the power cord
Material distinction between metal soleplate and plastic body
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the 'green' color of the steam holes. In real irons, holes are usually just dark voids or silver; green rims might indicate a specific model or an AI hallucination of 'functionality'. Check if the geometry of the holes is consistent (circular vs oval distortion) based on perspective.
